subject: history_social
passage: Many accounts portray the printing press as having made the handwritten book obsolete almost overnight. Granted, scribes did not vanish when Johannes Gutenberg's workshop in Mainz began printing in the 1450s: wealthy patrons went on commissioning illuminated manuscripts for decades, and some copyists even produced handwritten copies of printed books. ______ the overall shift was remarkably swift by the standards of the age, for by 1500 presses had been set up in well over two hundred European towns and had produced, by most estimates, millions of printed volumes.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence begins with "Granted," conceding that handwritten books lingered. The last sentence turns back to the main point: the shift to print was swift. After a concession, the writer needs a transition that returns to the main claim in spite of the point just conceded.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Granted" introduces a concession, but the last sentence is not another point against the main claim; it argues for the main claim. Using "Granted" again would mislabel it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The spread of presses to more than two hundred towns is not an example of scribes continuing to work; it points the other way.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar point, but the rapid spread of printing contrasts with the persistence of handwritten books described just before it.
explanation.D: Correct. "Still" signals that, despite the conceded persistence of scribes, the overall shift to print was fast.
